customManagers.description: Track the tag/ref of every version-pinned github flake input. The nix manager only advances flake.lock along the ref an input already tracks; it never rewrites the ref string in flake.nix, so a tag-pinned input reports nothing at all. Before this manager existed only playwright-web-flake was matched, and cilium-src, argocd-src, argocd-helm-src, gateway-api-src and sops-secrets-operator-src had never once been bumped since the commits that introduced them. The first pattern requires the ref to be an optional v followed by a dotted numeric version, which is what keeps this honest: it declines to match refs with no version (github:owner/repo, deliberate trunk tracking), branch refs (main, master, dev, writeShellApplication, future-26.11), fork labels (cognee-v112) and 40-hex revision pins (zen-browser, niri-flake), whose exactness modules/checks/pyrite-desktop.nix asserts on. dms-src is deliberately a release-tag pin and is matched here: pyrite-desktop.nix asserts that its tag equals the packaged dms-shell version, so a tag PR passes exactly when nixpkgs ships that release. The nix manager opens no digest PRs for it, because a ref-only input carries no original.rev and is left to lock-file maintenance, which is not enabled. Anchoring on .url also keeps .inputs.<x>.follows lines out. The second pattern is narrow on purpose: argo-helm publishes one tag series per chart, so its ref carries an argo-cd- prefix that no general version pattern can accept without also accepting branch names, and the packageRule below gives that one dependency a matching versioning scheme.

One dependency per package pin (openspec automate-package-version-bumps design D6): depName is the pin's name and its source tag selects the datasource. githubRelease reads github-releases for owner/repo with an extractVersion built from tagTemplate, its literal text regex-escaped and {version} as the version group; npm and pypi read their registries; vendorJson and vendorText read the custom datasource named custom.<name>, and a vendorText pin's regex is its extractVersion; gitCommit reads git-refs on its branch with the pin's version, which is the commit, as currentDigest, so a digest update rewrites the field realizedVersion is checked against. currentValue is the pin's version, or a gitCommit pin's branch. The realizer's test fixtures under pkgs/by-name/realize-pin/tests are excluded by config:recommended's ignorePaths.
matchStrings: {"depName": name, "currentValue": $exists(source.gitCommit) ? source.gitCommit.branch : version, "currentDigest": $exists(source.gitCommit) ? version, "datasource": $exists(source.githubRelease) ? "github-releases" : $exists(source.npm) ? "npm" : $exists(source.pypi) ? "pypi" : ($exists(source.vendorJson) or $exists(source.vendorText)) ? "custom." & name : $exists(source.gitCommit) ? "git-refs", "packageName": $exists(source.githubRelease) ? source.githubRelease.owner & "/" & source.githubRelease.repo : $exists(source.npm) ? source.npm.package : $exists(source.pypi) ? source.pypi.package : $exists(source.gitCommit) ? "https://github.com/" & source.gitCommit.owner & "/" & source.gitCommit.repo, "extractVersion": $exists(source.githubRelease) ? "^" & $join($map($split(source.githubRelease.tagTemplate, "{version}"), function($s) { $replace($s, /[\\.*+?^${}()|\[\]]/, function($m) { "\\" & $m.match }) }), "(?<version>.+)") & "$" : $exists(source.vendorText) ? source.vendorText.regex}

moshi-hook.description: moshi-hook's vendorText source: the url of pkgs/by-name/moshi-hook/pin.json, one line such as v0.4.64; the pin's regex is applied as extractVersion by the jsonata manager.

claude-code.description: claude-code's vendorText source: the url of pkgs/by-name/claude-code/pin.json, the bare version its latest pointer names; the pin's regex is applied as extractVersion by the jsonata manager.

dbt-fusion.description: dbt-fusion's vendorJson source: the url of pkgs/by-name/dbt-fusion/pin.json, whose pointer /latest/tag names the latest channel's tag, such as v2.0.13; the transform reads that tag and drops its leading v, so the single release is the bare version the pin holds.

devin-cli.description: devin-cli's vendorJson source: the url of pkgs/by-name/devin-cli/pin.json, the vendor's manifest of its latest release; the transform reads the pin's pointer /version as the one release Renovate sees.

impressive.description: impressive's vendorText source: the url of pkgs/by-name/impressive/pin.json, SourceForge's RSS listing of /Impressive, one <link> per line; the pin's regex is applied as extractVersion by the jsonata manager.

packageRules.description: Disable nix manager for playwright-web-flake to avoid conflict with custom regex manager

argo-helm tags every chart in one repository, so the argo-cd chart's tags read argo-cd-9.3.4 rather than 9.3.4. Under the default semver versioning that string is not a version at all, so the dependency would be extracted and then silently skipped. This regex versioning makes the whole tag the version: non-argo-cd tags in the same repository fail to parse and are discarded, and getNewValue returns the datasource's tag verbatim (lib/modules/versioning/generic.ts), so the prefix is preserved when the ref is rewritten.

One non-major PR for the JavaScript dependencies of the bun-managed workspace; bun itself is excluded, because its packageManager entry is disabled and follows nixpkgs (see the packageManager rule below). Every update of a dependency declared in package.json or packages/*/package.json regenerates the shared bun.lock (and, through the bun post-upgrade task below, bun.nix), so separate PRs conflict pairwise and land one per CI cycle. Matching the lock file rather than package names tracks the unit of conflict as dependencies come and go: the bun manager attaches the root bun.lock to every workspace member (lib/modules/manager/bun/extract.ts), and matchFileNames tests lock files as well as package files (lib/util/package-rules/files.ts). The coupled groups below override this one because later packageRules win, so a cloudflare-workers-tooling or astro update that breaks does not hold back routine ones; majors stay separate. npm playwright is not updated by the bun manager at all (see the playwright rules at the end).

The rust nightly channel is a derived constraint (aeneas -> charon pin -> required nightly), not a free-floating dependency; surface drift on the dependency dashboard but never open a PR automatically

@cloudflare/vite-plugin bundles an exact wrangler and emits config fields that a mismatched wrangler CLI rejects; bumping either alone breaks the docs build. Both are pinned exactly, the root override included: under a range, regenerating bun.lock for any other update re-resolves them, so a nested newer wrangler (as @cloudflare/vitest-plugin brings) can be hoisted into the CLI that deploy-docs runs and an unrelated PR inherits its behaviour changes. Pinned, only this group moves the deploy toolchain, and the deploy-docs rehearsal judges it here.

Move astro, its integrations and starlight in one PR. Renovate's built-in monorepo preset already groups astro with @astrojs/* because they share the withastro/astro repository, but @astrojs/starlight lives in withastro/starlight, so it arrives in a PR of its own. That is not a merge-order inconvenience, it is a broken tree: @astrojs/starlight 0.42.2 declares peerDependencies astro ^7.2.10 and @astrojs/markdown-remark ^7.3.0, while this repo pins astro 7.2.9 and @astrojs/markdown-remark ^7.2.4, and the resulting build fails with "@astrojs/markdown-remark is too old to render .mdx files". The grouping criterion here is a shared peer-dependency floor, not a shared upstream repository. @astrojs/** deliberately includes @astrojs/cloudflare, which has peers on both astro ^7.2.0 and wrangler ^4.125.0 and so straddles this group and cloudflare-workers-tooling: packageRules are applied in array order and a later match overwrites an earlier one, so placing this rule after the cloudflare rule makes the astro group the deliberate winner. The astro floor is the one that breaks the build on a minor bump; the wrangler floor is a caret range that any 4.x satisfies, and a wrangler major would surface as a docs build failure rather than a silent mismatch.

conventional-changelog-conventionalcommits@10 requires conventional-changelog-writer@9, which semantic-release@25's bundled @semantic-release/release-notes-generator@14 does not resolve; hold on 9.x until semantic-release ships a compatible generator

semantic-release 26 requires Node >=26.13, while the release app runs nixpkgs' default Node 24, and 26.0.1 depends on beta plugins (@semantic-release/core, commit-analyzer, npm and release-notes-generator prereleases). Hold on 25.x; revisit when its plugins are stable.

lazyvim-nix v16.0.2 links each Nix-managed plugin into the dev path as <owner>--<repo> (pfassina/lazyvim-nix#115); lazy.nvim derives a plugin's name from that directory, so require() of a lazy plugin returns its module without loading it and lualine's config fails at every Neovim start. flake.nix holds v16.0.1; skip only the broken tag, so a later tag that fixes it (pfassina/lazyvim-nix#117, #119) is still proposed.

bun is derived, not tracked: the packageManager field must equal the nixpkgs bun that renovate's bun post-upgrade task runs, or a different bun can rewrite bun.lock. The renovate aspect (modules/nixos/renovate.nix) asserts the pairing, so a flake.lock bump that moves nixpkgs bun must carry the packageManager edit. Renovate never proposes it on its own.

Typst @preview package versions follow nixpkgs typstPackages: the docs build compiles diagrams offline with typst.withPackages (modules/nixpkgs/overlays/typst.nix), so an import of a version nixpkgs does not ship fails in the sandbox. Bump the imports alongside a flake.lock update that brings the package. Renovate never proposes them on its own.
Regex-manager flake.nix ref bumps never touch flake.lock; re-lock in the same commit so nixbot evaluates a complete tree.
bun manager updates bun.lock; regenerate bun.nix from it in the same commit.

npm playwright is derived, not tracked: its version must equal the playwright-web-flake driver (pkgs/by-name/vanixiets-docs/package.nix guards the browsers.json revision match). Renovate never proposes it on its own.

A playwright-web-flake ref bump re-locks the flake, re-pins npm playwright to the new driver version, reconciles bun.lock and regenerates bun.nix in one commit. Both coordinates are listed so a fork-drop keeps the rule. Must stay after the custom.regex rule: postUpgradeTasks is not mergeable, so this object replaces that one.

The pin rule (openspec automate-package-version-bumps design D7): one branch renovate/

per package, whose single task runs the realizer for the proposed version. Renovate commits only the task's writes that match fileFilters and drops the rest silently, so the globs cover every path the realizer's write confinement (design D5) can admit for any pin: its pin.json, an apmRef companion's apm.yml under modules/home/ai/plugins, a fixedOutputHash companion's pkgs/by-name//hashes.json, and a remoteSkillHashes companion's pkgs/by-name/apm-skills-compose/skills.json; checks.renovate-allowed-commands fails when a pin or companion path falls outside them. separateMajorMinor false gives each package one PR straight to its newest version: with separate buckets, the major and non-major updates of one package share the branch renovate/

that branchTopic names, and Renovate kept one of them. allowedVersions admits only versions with a dot, since a floating release such as uncomment's v3 names no fixed artifact and semver-coerced versioning reads it as 3.0.0. The pin rule has no schedule: the instance runs hourly (modules/nixos/renovate.nix), at most 4 pin PRs are created in a clock hour, and the number open at once is unbounded, so the bound on magnetite's load is the rate, prHourlyLimit here and the instance's global prCommitsPerRunLimit of 4. Merge authorization stays with the operator: no automerge, and ignoreUnstable is left at its default.

Commit pins (openspec automate-package-version-bumps design D7, stage 2 wave 5): a gitCommit pin's update is a git-refs digest update to the head of its branch, for which newVersion is empty, so the task passes newDigest, the commit the realizer writes as the pin's version. postUpgradeTasks are not merged across rules, so this task replaces the pin rule's, with the same fileFilters and executionMode; checks.renovate-allowed-commands renders it with each gitCommit pin. The window, Monday 14:00 to 15:59 UTC with updateNotScheduled false, confines a commit pin's branch creation and rebases to the two hourly runs that fall in it each week: the skill repositories commit most days, every update rebuilds the home closures, and minimumReleaseAge cannot space them because git-refs releases carry no timestamp.

Label a pin's major update for review (openspec automate-package-version-bumps design D7). With separateMajorMinor false the pin rule raises one PR per package to its newest version, which may cross a major; Renovate still classifies the update as major (lib/workers/repository/process/lookup/generate.ts), so this rule can mark it.

Pins that run as stateful services on fleet hosts are upgraded only after operator approval (openspec automate-package-version-bumps design D7, permanent): greptimedb-bin is services.greptimedb.package on magnetite, and a new version may change its storage format, so data it writes may not be readable after a downgrade. Before approving, read the upstream release notes for storage-format and compatibility changes, run the VM tests that exercise the store (greptimedb-pipeline, fleet-ingress, devloop-ingest), and plan magnetite's deploy with a rollback that accounts for that downgrade incompatibility. perses-bin is services.perses.package on magnetite, whose database holds the dashboards; before approving, read its release notes for database and plugin compatibility changes and run the perses-greptimedb VM test.

atomic is held for operator approval (openspec automate-package-version-bumps design D10): since 0.10.4 the @bastani/atomic npm tarball ships no npm-shrinkwrap.json, so realize-pin cannot pin its dependency tree and a realization fails at npm ci. The hold stays until upstream ships a lockfile again or atomic is built from the upstream monorepo at its release tag.
